documentation.value: Textual description of the item's dimensions.

Formula for obtaining values.
Additional Information: The possible values are monetary values, ranking scores, criterion weighting.

properties.documentation:
Name given by an organisation to its product or service, or range of products or services.
Additional information: Brand name allows economic operators to distinctively describe an item in their eCatalogue. This may be different from the "item name".

documentation.value: External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/title

properties.documentation: A phase-agnostic Document describing a set of Items offered for purchase that can be processed in an electronic way.

documentation.value:
Information about payment conditions applied to all items in the catalogue.
Additional information: This property may need to be used together with the payment arrangements provided in the ContractTerms, where such terms exists.

properties.documentation:
Information about fee or duty imposed.
Additional Information: Charge category indicates the nature of the duty/fee, for example CAR, etc. Charge category modifier may be used in case different levels, exemptions or other modifications apply. The charge can be fixed or relative to the price.
Combination of two Items where the former enhances the latter.
Combination of two Items which mutually enhance one another.

Inclusion of an Item into in the described Item.
Additional Information: The Item is provided with its components, however, the component Items may also be provided separately. For example, a bicycle has wheels as components, but they may be provided as spare parts as well. This relation is useful to describe different package levels of an item or hierarchies of Items.
Construct meant to represent the association between an attribute defined in an external classification scheme and the value ascribed to it.

documentation.value: External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/title

The property defined in a classification scheme.
Additional Information: For example, the following two properties are defined in the ECLASS classification of goods and services: (0173-1#02-AAA026#007) drilling diameter: drilling diameter, (0173-1#02-AAA030#007) flange diameter: flange diameter .

The classification scheme where a property is defined.
Additional Information: For example, the following two properties are defined in the ECLASS classification of goods and services: (0173-1#02-AAA026#007) drilling diameter: drilling diameter, (0173-1#02-AAA030#007) flange diameter: flange diameter .

Simple value of the property, which is defined in a classification scheme.
Additional Information: For example, the (0173-1#02-AAV139#001) coating 1 of an optical material has value of "silver".
This simple literal value is for the cases when the property value does not have units, in which case the qualifiedValue shall be used.

properties.documentation:
A specific design or version of a product or service.
Additional information: This class is meant as a reusable reference to the model name rather than as a set of specifications of an Item of this particular model.

documentation.value: External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/title

properties.documentation: Connection between two Items.

documentation.value: The number or the fraction of a related item.

properties.documentation: Supplantment, displacement or suspension of an Item by the described Item.

Necessity of an Item by the described item.
Additional Information: The described item is provided without other items that are required for proper functionality.
For example, a printer cannot be used without ink cartridge; or a Server cannot be used without its installation.

Amount of money required or given in exchange for Items.
Additional information: The Price excludes any charges (such as taxes, duties and fees) and discounts.
Document providing information about an Item.

The Producer of goods or provider of services.
Additional Information: Also, known as Supplier and Manufacturer.
We do not care who provides these service or products we care with whom Business is done.
PEPPOL - Invoice: The Supplier is the Legal Person or Organisation who provides a product and/or service.
PEPPOL - Order: The supplier is the legal person or organisation who provides a product or service. Examples of supplier roles: seller, despatch party, creditor, economic operator.
A Document describing a set of Items offered for purchase that can be processed in an electronic way, after a Contract is signed.

Aggregated information about the Terms and specifications for procuring an Item.
Details about an Item, like Prices, packaging, discounts, special promotions, etc.
TC 440:
Detailed information of an Item, Price and its composition in a Catalogue.
Composition: e.g. information referring to its description, how to order it, what it is made of, properties, delivery conditions, etc.

documentation.value: Orderable quantity increment: The increment of Orderable units that can be ordered.
The factor by which the Item net price of an unit of an item can be converted to the orderable unit.
Textual description of the specific transaction conditions (purchasing, sales, payment, delivery) for an item.
Warranty information that applies to the catalogue line item.
Indicator if the item is offered in accordance to an existing contract.
Indicator, if the item is orderable or not, e.g. because it is temporarily out of stock.

properties.documentation: A production Lot in which the Item instances were produced.

documentation.value: The day until which the quality of the item will remain optimal.
The last day until which the item can be used.
The day of production.

properties.documentation:
A product, work, service or any combination of them.
Additional Information: An Item can be an atomic Thing or a composition of things that together are seen as a unit, e.g. a tetrabrik of milk or an indivisible package of six tetrabriks.
No distinction is provided between services, goods and works to leave room for innovation.

External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/title
List of words (e.g, synonyms) to make the item searchable.
Indicator whether an item is in the supplier's stock. If not in stock the supplier has to order the item.

Peppol used the UNCL5387 list for this purpose:
https://docs.peppol.eu/pracc/catalogue/1.0/codelist/UNCL5387/ https://service.unece.org/trade/untdid/d95b/uncl/uncl5387.htm
Additional Information: https://service.unece.org/trade/untdid/d97a/uncl/uncl5305.htm
Additional Information: https://service.unece.org/trade/untdid/d00a/tred/tred5153.htm

This is a controlled list indicating whether an Item is a product or service.
Additional information: For example possible values could be: * SER - Trade Item is a service * MTO - Trade Item is manufactured after Order * VQ - Trade Item is variable measure Item, that is, the Quantity in the package is not fixed, and the Price for the Item varies with the Quantity * RC - Trade Item is a returnable unit
For example the list of possible Item types is available here: https://www.gs1.org/sites/default/files/docs/eancom/ean02s4/part3/dc245.htm

This reference stands for a context dependent controlled list: CPV, UNSPC, UNCL7143 (for ordering)
Needs to be aligned with eCatalogue in order to chose a codelist to be used.

Waiting for code list.
Code that defines how the line should be applied to an existing eCatalogue.
Additional information:
Catalogue: Legal codes on Catalogue header level:
Add – Used when a catalogue is sent for the first time to the Catalogue Receiver referring to the contract in the header of the catalogue. Replace – Replaces the entire catalogue referring to the contract. This is the default action. Update – Updates a current catalogue. Delete – deletes the entire catalogue
Catalogue lines:
Add – Used to add items to the catalogue. Update – Used to update an item. The entire Catalogue Line is updated. Only used if Action code on header level is Update Delete – Used to delete an entire Catalogue line. Only used if Action code on header level is Update.
Waiting for code list.
Waiting for code list.

Grouping of data that may be associated to various concepts.
Additional Information: For example, AllowanceChargeInformation may be associated to the Order or the Catalogue (either at the Line level or at the Document level), amongst others.

documentation.value: External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/description
Supplementary data about the instance of the concept.

properties.documentation:
A formal reply from the Catalogue Receiver to the Catalogue Provider stating the Catalogue Receiver's ability to apply the catalogue for placing orders.
Additional Information: The Catalogue Response is used to inform on the acceptance or rejection of a Catalogue.

documentation.value: Explanation of the response.

properties.documentation:
Details concerning the Catalogue Receiver’s ability to apply a given Catalogue Line for placing orders.
Additional information: The Catalogue Response Line is used to inform on the acceptance or rejection of a Catalogue Line.

documentation.value: Explanation of the response.
The relation indicating until when a given instance of a concept is applicable.
Information that is particular to one or multiple Order Lines.
The total cost for moving the goods.

Qualified value of the property, which is defined in a classification scheme.
Additional Information: For example, the (0173-1#02-AAA026#007) drilling diameter of an item has value of 12 inches.
The minimum quantity of the item that can be ordered to the given net monetary value.
The expected amount of time between the order and delivery of an item.
The period of time when the Item can be ordered to the given price.
The price amount of an Item exclusive of taxes and after substracting price discounts.
The quantity at which the net monetary value applies.

The factor by which the base unit of the price can be converted to orderable unit.
Additional information: This is needed when the base price is provided different than the orderable unit. For example, when selling paper, the price may be set per page, but the orderable unit is a package of 500 pieces. Therefore the price needs to be converted to the orderable unit.
Location delivery area where the Item can be ordered to the given price.

The item price based on a standardised unit.
Additional Information: The unit must be indicated in the Quantity, with a quantity value of 1.
The manufacturer's identifier for the item.
The product maker or service provider.

Additional information: If an order refers to multiple catalogues then all these catalogues ideally are subordinated to the same contract. Some countries however may allow multiple contracts per order (i.e Italy).
Coded description of the specific transaction conditions (purchasing, sales, payment, delivery) for an item.
The unit in which the item described in this catalogue line can be ordered.
The relation indicating until when a Catalogue Line instance is applicable.
The minimum quantity of an item that is guaranteed by the seller to be delivered.
The maximum number of orderable units that can be ordered according to details provided in the catalogue line, such as price.
Additional Information: The reference to the catalogue line is for information only, to trace the source of the information provided in the order line.
The identifier assigned to a specific batch of the produced Item.

The source country of the product or service.
Additional Information:
The country of origin can be provided by the buyer as a requirement or by the tenderer information of the item to be provided.

The general identifier assigned to the concept based on a standard scheme.​
Additional information: For example the GTIN scheme (Global Trade Item Number).
Specification of the hazardous nature of an item according to a classification schema. Provides detail of the classification and nature of a hazardous item.
The net quantity of the item that is contained in each consumable unit, excluding any packaging materials.
External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/hasPart
An additional item that can enhance the original item.
Relation to the proof of conformance.

A classification of this item according to a specific system for classifying products or services.
Additional information: Examples of classification schemes are: CPV, UNSPC, eCl@ss, GPC, ...
The general identifier assigned to the concept as defined by the Seller.​
Specification of the hazardous nature of an item according to the UNDG classification schema. Provides detail of the classification and nature of a hazardous item.

An item that if used with another item provides mutual enhancements to both of them.
Additional information: For example, gin and tonic; or smart-phone and smart-watch.
External concept defined by https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/isReplacedBy
The identifier assigned to the specific instance of the produced concept.
The general identifier assigned to the concept as defined by the Manufacturer. ​
The general identifier assigned to the concept as defined by the Buyer.​
Is related to a Document.

An identifier assigned by the Buyer used for internal routing purposes.
A universally unique identifier for an instance of this document.
